The updated standard is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2024. Early adoption is permitted. The Company adopted this guidance for the annual period ending December 31, 2025, using the retrospective approach. The enhanced disclosures can be found in Note 12 - </span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Income Taxes.</span></p><p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</span></p><p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">In December 2025, the FASB issued ASU No. 2025-12</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">,</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Codification Improvements</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> to address suggestions received from stakeholders on the Accounting Standards Codification (the "Codification") and to make other incremental improvements to U.S. GAAP. The update represents changes to the Codification that clarify, correct errors in or make other improvements to a variety of topics that are intended to make it easier to understand and apply. The amendments to this update are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2026 and interim periods within those annual reporting periods. The Company is currently evaluating the impact that the updated standard will have on its financial statements.</span></p><p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">In December 2025, the FASB issued ASU No. 2025-11, </span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Interim Reporting (Topic 270): Narrow - Scope Improvements</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">. The update provides clarifications intended to improve the consistency and usability of interim disclosure requirements, including a comprehensive listing of required interim disclosures and a new disclosure principle for reporting material events occurring after the most recent annual period. The amendments do not change the underlying objectives of interim reporting but are designed to enhance clarity in application. The amendments to this update are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2027 and interim periods within those annual reporting periods. The Company is currently evaluating the impact that the updated standard will have on its financial statements.</span></p><p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">In December 2025, the FASB issued ASU No. 2025-10, </span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Government Grants (Topic 832): Accounting for Government Grants Received by Business Entities</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">. The amendments in this update establish the accounting for a government grant received by a business entity, including guidance for (1) a grant related to an asset and (2) a grant related to income. A grant related to an asset is a government grant, or part of a government grant, that is conditioned on the purchase, construction, or acquisition of an asset (for example, a long-lived asset or inventory). A grant related to income is a government grant, or part of a government grant, other than a grant related to an asset (for example, a grant that reimburses a business entity for operating expenses). The amendments in this update require that a government grant received by a business entity should not be recognized until it is probable that (a) a business entity will comply with the conditions attached to the grant and (b) the grant will be received, and the business entity meets the recognition guidance for a grant related to <br/>an asset or a grant related to income. The amendments to this update are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2028 and interim periods within those reporting periods. The Company is currently evaluating the impact that the updated standard will have on its financial statements.</span></p><p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-06 -</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software.</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> The amendment simplifies the capitalization guidance by removing all references to software development project stages so that</span><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div></ix:continuation></div></div>

that the frustration of purpose doctrine excuses the Company&#8217;s performance; and that the Lease is terminated or that the Company is entitled to receive an abatement of rent due to the lack of tenantability of the leased premises. On August 6, 2025, Crown filed an Answer and Counterclaim in which it seeks a declaration from the Court that the Company is in breach because the Lease imposes on the Company the responsibility to obtain and maintain certain utility services. Crown is seeking actual and consequential damages for the Company&#8217;s alleged breach of failing to obtain certain utility services, including, but not limited to, diminution of value of the property, cost associated with providing water and wastewater service to the Property, reimbursement of tenant improvements paid by Crown for the Company&#8217;s occupancy, contractual indemnity for and all other damages caused by the Company&#8217;s alleged breach, plus rent due under the Lease and costs of reletting the property if the Company is forced to vacate prior to the Lease term, as well as costs and attorney&#8217;s fees. Discovery is ongoing in the matter. The Company believes that it is not possible at this time to reasonably assess the outcome of this matter or to estimate the loss or range of losses, if any, as the matter is in early stages.</span></p><p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Other Matters</span></p><p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">In the future, PCT may become party to additional legal matters and claims arising in the ordinary course of business. While PCT is unable to predict the outcome of the above or future matters, it does not believe, based upon currently available facts, that the ultimate resolution of any such pending matters will have
